extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and attorneys filing or prosecuting patent applications before the IPOPHL (Philippines)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and formal requirements for preparing, filing, and prosecuting patent applications before the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL), including drawings, claims, fees, agents, filing date formalities, unity/divisional practice, and working models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters and Figures of Reference (Rule 414.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The different views shall be consecutively numbered. Letters and figures of reference must be carefully formed and should, if possible, measure at least 3.2 mm in height so that they may bear reduction to 1.06 mm; may be larger when space allows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place reference letters/figures in close and complex parts so as not to interfere with comprehension; rarely cross or mingle with lines; when grouped place at a little distance and connect by lines; not placed on shaded surfaces (leave blank in shading if unavoidable); all numbers/letters/reference lines shall be simple and clear; do not use brackets, circles, or inverted commas with numbers/letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Placement on Drawings (Rule 414.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The name and signature of the applicant or authorized representative should be placed at the lower right hand corner within the imaginary margins of each sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures must not trespass upon the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position of Large Views on Drawing Sheets (Rule 414.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different figures shall be arranged on sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably in an upright position, clearly separated from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figures longer than sheet width are necessary they shall be presented sideways with the top of the figures at the left side of the sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow Sheets and Diagrams as Drawings (Rule 414.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow sheets and diagrams may be considered drawings provided they serve as an aid in the clear understanding of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites for the Figure in the IPOPHL E‑Gazette (Rule 414.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, only one view of each invention can be shown in the IPOPHL E‑Gazette illustrations; the selected view must show the nature of the invention or its specific improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The figure may be a perspective, plan, side or sectional view, according to the judgment of the Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Signs Consistency (Rule 414.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference signs not mentioned in the description and claims shall not appear in the drawings and vice versa; the same feature must be denoted by the same sign throughout description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings contain many reference signs, strongly recommended to attach a separate sheet listing all reference signs and the features denoted by them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs (Rule 414.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Photographs are not normally proper drawings but acceptable for obtaining a filing date and are informal drawings. (b) Photographs submitted online must be clear, adequately illustrate the invention, preferably black-and-white; color allowed if clearer. (c–d) For manual filings, black-and-white photographs/photomicrographs printed on sensitized paper may be accepted in lieu of India ink drawings for inventions not accurately depicted by drafting; paper must meet generally recognized trade characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must show the invention more clearly than India ink drawings and otherwise comply with rules concerning drawings; photolithographs or screened reproductions are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters Not Permitted on Drawings (Rule 414.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stamp of an agent or attorney, advertisement, or written address shall not be permitted on the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonconforming Drawings Accepted Conditionally (Rule 414.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: A drawing not executed in conformity with the rules may be admitted for examination if it sufficiently illustrates the invention, but must be corrected or replaced before allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to employ a competent draftsman to make their drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing Requisites (Rule 415)
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets of the sequence listing must be numbered sequentially relative to each other, the series appearing in the center of either the top or bottom margins, using Arabic numerals separated by '/' (e.g., '1/5').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may submit sequence listing in PDF saved on CD-ROM if manually filed application contains a sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Must Conclude the Application (Rule 416(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application must conclude with a claim, particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the part, improvement, or combination regarded as the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and Dependent Claims; Clarity and Support (Rule 416(b–d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application may contain one or more independent claims in the same category; each claim shall be clear, concise, and supported by the description. Dependent claims may refer back and further limit another claim; multiple dependent claims must refer in the alternative only and cannot serve as a basis for other multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must conform to the invention as set forth in the description; terms and phrases used in claims must have clear support/antecedent basis in the description so their meaning is ascertainable by reference to the description; claims shall not, except where absolutely necessary, rely on reference to the description or drawings (avoid 'as described in part xxx').

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for Improvements (Rule 416(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention relates to an improvement, claims should specifically point out and distinctly claim the improvement in combination with a preamble indicating prior art features necessary for the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Contents of Claims — Structure (Rule 417)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought in terms of technical features. Where appropriate, claims shall contain: (a) a statement indicating designation and prior art technical features necessary for definition; (b) a characterizing portion preceded by 'characterized in that' or 'characterized by' stating the technical features to be protected; (c) if drawings present, technical features may be followed by reference signs in parentheses (not construed as limiting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Incurring Fee (Rule 418)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application with more than five (5) claims (independent or multiple/alternative dependent) at filing or added after filing incurs payment of a claims fee for each claim over five; fee payable in full upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims fee is deficient applicant may pay within one month grace after notice; unpaid fees lead to deemed deletion of claim(s). Multiple dependent claims are counted as the number of claims to which direct reference is made; claims depending on multiple dependent claims are counted accordingly. Markush/genus/species claims incur fees computed depending on number of enumerated members/variations. Multiple dependent claims and original applications filed with multiple dependent claims require additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of Application Documents — General (Rule 419(a–j))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers for an application must be original copy only, legibly written/typewritten/printed in permanent ink on one side; typing 1½-spaced; capital letters not less than 0.21 cm and in dark indelible color. Documents on A4 (29.7 x 21 cm) paper, pliable, strong, white, smooth, matte, durable. Abstract, description and claims lines must be numbered in sets of five restarting each page (numbers on left margin). Each document commences on a separate sheet. Margins specified and must be blank. Abstract/description/claims/drawings/sequence listings filed online may be in separate files per system; copies required if voluminous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables and chemical/mathematical formulas allowed; may be presented sideways if necessary with top at left side. Physical values in SI units where appropriate; use technical terms/signs/symbols generally accepted in the field. Page numbering rules: abstract/description/claims pages numbered consecutively with Arabic numerals in central top or bottom margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Models When Required (Rule 420)
rubrics_metrics.description: A working model may be required to demonstrate operation to enable the Office to fully understand the precise operation of a machine if the invention cannot be sufficiently described in the application; Examiner will notify applicant and requirement constitutes official action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presented, workability assessment, dates of presentation/demonstration/filing entered in file wrapper; models not required nor admitted will be returned to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites for the Working Model (Rule 420.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When required, working model must clearly exhibit every feature of the machine which forms the subject of the claim(s) of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model should not include other matters beyond the actual invention unless necessary to exhibit the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action when Model Required (Rule 420.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a working model is required, applicant may file a request for suspension of action upon full payment of prescribed fee; suspension period shall not exceed six (6) months from filing such request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit the working model within the prescribed period shall cause the application to be deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material Required for the Model (Rule 420.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The model must be neatly and substantially made of durable material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the material forms an essential feature of the invention, the model should be constructed of that material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models Returned to Applicant (Rule 420.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications refused or withdrawn, the working model, unless necessary to be preserved in the Office, may be returned to the applicant upon demand and at his expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant Visit and Inspection (Rule 420.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If presenting a working model is not possible (e.g., large machines), applicant may request a plant visit and inspection for assessment of workability; the Examiner shall conduct the visit and make a report forming part of the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant shall shoulder expenses incurred during the visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of Attorney‑at‑Law or Patent Agent Recommended (Rule 421)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may prosecute his own case but is advised, unless familiar, to employ a competent attorney-at-law or patent agent because the value of patents depends largely on skillful preparation of description and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot aid in selection of an attorney or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Appointment of Resident Agent for Non‑Residents (Rule 422)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who is not a resident of the Philippines must appoint and maintain a Philippine resident agent or representative upon whom issuances, office actions, notices, or processes may be served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to appoint within one (1) month from office issuance directing appointment shall cause the application to be deemed withdrawn (applies to direct route and PCT national phase entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents or Representatives on Record (Rule 422.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall contain the name and contact details of the patent agent or representative. A representative/agent shall be authorized to transact prosecution/maintenance and address all communications/notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more agents appointed, Office forwards actions to the last agent appointed on record. Substitute/associate attorney may be appointed by an attorney only upon written authorization of principal; a third attorney appointed by the second will not be recognized. Power of attorney may be revoked at any stage upon proper notification; upon revocation Office communicates directly with applicant or new attorney/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Address of Applicant or Agent (Rule 422.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant, agent, or representative must inform the Office of any change in their address or email address on record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to receive communications due to failure to inform Office of address change shall not be accepted as justifiable ground in subsequent responses, submissions, requests, or petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum and Courtesy Required (Rule 423(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys/agents are required to conduct business with the Office with professionalism, politeness, decorum, and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who violate this Rule shall be required to be represented by an attorney; papers in violation will be submitted to the Director and returned to the sender by direct order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints Against Examiners on Separate Paper (Rule 423(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints against Examiners and other officers must be made in a communication separate from other papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such complaints will be promptly investigated by or at the instance of the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Apply for a Patent (Rule 500)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, natural or juridical, may apply for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is not the inventor, proof of authority to apply for the patent is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Applicant Dies, Becomes Insane, or Incapacitated (Rule 501)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant dies, becomes insane, or incapacitated, the legally appointed administrator, executor, guardian, conservator, or representative may sign application papers and may apply for and obtain the patent in the name of the applicant, heirs, or assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned Invention and Patents (Rule 502)
rubrics_metrics.description: If whole interest in invention is assigned, application may be filed by or in name of assignee who may sign; if assignee is juridical person, any officer may sign; for aliquot/undivided interests any joint owner may sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Juridical Person (Rule 503)
rubrics_metrics.description: A juridical person is a body of persons, corporation, partnership, or any legal entity recognized by law with personality separate from shareholders/partners/members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Authority (Rule 504)
rubrics_metrics.description: If person signing on behalf of a juridical person is an officer, no proof required; if another person signs, Office requires proof of authority (e.g., Special Power of Attorney). For electronic filings the same rule applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of Signature Accepted (Rule 505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a signature is required, Office may accept hand‑written signature or other forms such as printed/stamped signature, use of a seal, or thumb marks accompanied by an indication in letters of the signatory's name; any form recognized as valid under Philippine law is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No attestation, notarization, legalization, Apostille, or other certification required except where signature concerns voluntary withdrawal, surrender of letters patent, assignment of rights, and other submissions required to be sworn and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Date Requirements (Rule 600)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date shall be the date on which the Office received the following elements in English or Filipino: (a) a duly accomplished request expressly indicating a Philippine patent is sought; (b) an abstract; (c) description; (d) at least one claim; (e) drawings, if necessary; (f) payment of required fees at time of filing; (g) appointment of agent if applicant is non‑resident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete Application — Drawings Timing (Rule 600.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application refers to drawing(s), it is not considered complete if drawings are not included, but drawings may be filed within one (1) month from filing without need for notification and will not affect filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing via Resident Agent — Copy Receipt (Rule 600.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For obtaining a filing date for applications filed through a resident agent, Office may receive a copy of application by telefax or e-mail, provided the original is submitted within one (1) month from the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: According a Filing Date Procedure (Rule 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office examines whether application satisfies filing date requirements (Rule 400 and Rule 600). If complete, filing date is: (a) date of receipt in IPOPHL electronic filing system; (b) mailing date stamped by Post Office or courier; (c) date of actual receipt if filed manually; (d) date stamped received by IPSOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incomplete Office issues Office Action identifying deficiencies and gives applicant opportunity to correct. If deficiencies not remedied within one (1) month from initial presentation application considered forfeited and a Notice of Forfeited Application issued. Application forfeited for filing date deficiencies shall not be published and may be filed anew. For incompleteness re appointment of resident agent Rule 422 applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality Examination Scope (Rule 602)
rubrics_metrics.description: If application accorded filing date and required fee paid in full, application shall be evaluated for formality requirements such as: (a) contents of request for grant; (b) priority documents if claiming convention priority; (c) proof of authority, if applicant not inventor; (d) deed of assignment; (e) full payment of other fees (e.g., deficit claims fees); (f) signature; (g) identification of the inventor; (h) formal drawings; (i) complete and clear description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late‑filed or Missing Drawings (Rule 603)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If drawings missing but submitted within one (1) month from filing, Office sends notice drawings and references deemed accepted for examination. (b) If submitted beyond one (1) month, Office notifies drawings and references shall be deemed deleted unless applicant requests within one (1) month that application be granted a new filing date (the date missing drawings were filed). (c) If drawings not filed, Office requires filing within one (1) month and informs applicant application will be given new filing date when complete or references to drawings will be deemed deleted if not filed. (d) New filing date cited in succeeding correspondences. Additional drawings beyond original disclosure filed after filing date denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Invention Requirement (Rule 604)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions forming a single general inventive concept (Sec. 38.1, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several independent inventions not forming a single general inventive concept are claimed, Director may require restriction to a single invention. A later divisional filed for divided out invention shall be considered filed same day as earlier application if filed within four (4) months after requirement to divide becomes final (or additional time up to two months under Rule 928b), and divisional shall not go beyond disclosure in initial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Grant Despite Lack of Unity Not Ground for Cancellation (Rule 604.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a patent has been granted on an application that did not comply with unity of invention shall not be a ground to cancel the patent (Sec. 38.3, IP Code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Unity of Invention — Technical Relationship (Rule 605)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity requirement fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among those inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. 'Special technical features' mean those features that define a contribution which each claimed invention makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of single general inventive concept made without regard to whether inventions are claimed separately or as alternatives in a single claim. Plurality of independent claims in different categories (product/process/apparatus/use) may constitute a group linked as a single general inventive concept. Examples provided for permissible different specific combinations of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of Requirement for Division (Rule 606)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disagrees with requirement of division, a request for reconsideration and withdrawal or modification may be filed giving reasons; applicant must indicate provisional election of one invention for prosecution which becomes the election if requirement becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement will be reconsidered; if repeated and made final Examiner will act on claims of elected invention; if final and applicant failed to indicate provisional election, the first group of claims indicated in office action will be considered for prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from Requirement for Division (Rule 607)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final requirement for division, applicant may appeal together with full payment of prescribed fee and subject to appeal rules; prosecution on elected invention may continue during appeal; final action or allowance deferred until appeal resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal may not be allowed if reconsideration of requirement was not requested. Applicant may request that the four (4) month period to file a divisional begin after appeal resolution, subject to payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent Presentation of Claims for Different Invention (Rule 608)
rubrics_metrics.description: If after an official action applicant presents claim(s) directed to an invention divisible from previously claimed invention, such claims, if amendment entered, will be refused and applicant required to limit claims to the invention previously claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Species (Rule 609)
rubrics_metrics.description: In first action on application containing a generic claim and multiple species claims, if after complete search Examiner holds no generic claim allowable, applicant shall be required to elect species to which claim shall be restricted if no generic claim finally allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed neither to species nor genus may be accepted. Markush type claims enumerating alternatives may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Divisional Applications — Timing and Priority (Rule 610)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mandatory divisional application arises from restriction following lack of unity. A divisional may give rise to more divisionals. A divisional will be examined same manner as parent and shall have benefit of priority of earlier application provided it is filed within four (4) months from date requirement for division made final or after an appeal resolved; periods for succeeding divisionals are counted from election or from final requirement date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four (4) month prescriptive period reckoned from mailing date of action or notice of decision to appeal; succeeding divisionals' periods counted from date of election or when requirement becomes final.
